# PROCESS — what I did this iteration (explainability; REQUIRED)

**Iteration 5/5 (final) · candidate `cand_0005` · parent `cand_0003` (champion, val 0.975, 39/40) ·
bar: paired Δ̄ > 0.2·SE = 0.0072 (SE 0.0358, n=40). Fixing the one failing task is worth
Δ̄ = +0.025 — 3.5× the bar. Breaking one passing task cancels it exactly. So this iteration is a
*precision* iteration, not a breadth iteration: there is only one failing task and the entire
difficulty is shipping its fix without the collateral that sank `cand_0004`.**

## The situation this iteration inherits

```
RESULT cand_0004: REJECTED · val=0.975 Δ=+0.000 · fixed={59595} · broke={50768}
```

`cand_0004` *solved* the target task and lost the iteration to a single collateral regression. Its
whole batch was reverted. So the deliverable here is not "which task fails" (one, 59595) — it is
**which of `cand_0004`'s five edits broke 50768**, so the fixing text can be reshipped and the
breaking text left out. I built that attribution from artifacts, not inference:

- the *post-edit* trace `rollouts/val/50768__cand_0004__t0.json` (the actual failing run), compared
  line by line against `rollouts/val/50768__cand_0003__t0.json` (the passing run);
- `rollouts/val/59595__cand_0003__t0.json` (the failing run I must fix);
- a full `diff` of `work/cand_0004/{prompt.md,task_template.md}` against the champion's (the copied
  `prior_iterations/cand_0004/diff.patch` is **truncated** mid-hunk and cannot be used alone);
- a mechanical audit over all 40 champion traces of save-count and `changed`-sequence.

Three read-only subagents did the three deep reads in parallel (see "Process/features used").

## No ENVIRONMENT fault

Every one of the 40 traces runs to completion, `error: None` throughout, grader feedback consistent
across all five candidates. Both moves (59595 up, 50768 down) are fully explained by text in the two
editable files. Nothing outside `prompt.md` and `task_template.md` was touched or needs to be.

## Ranked failure/risk list

Only one task fails, so leverage ranking collapses; what actually needed ranking was the *risk*.

| # | cluster | tasks | tag | leverage | recoverable |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | **Verified answer discarded in a later round** — the agent computes the gold answer, the readback is all-clear, then it spends a spare round writing the cells' *original* contents back | 59595 (reward 0.00) | **STRUCTURE** (+ a CONFLICT it rests on) | 1 task × 1 trial × 1.00 | +0.025 paired, bar 0.0072 |
| 2 | **Grid axis transposed because the axis TITLES were never read** — the regression channel that cancelled `cand_0004` | 50768 (passes at 1.0; failed under `cand_0002` *and* `cand_0004`) | **CAPABILITY-GAP / METHOD** | regression-hardening, not a new win | protects −0.025 |

### Cluster 1, root cause (verbatim from the trace)

Round 2 of 59595 wrote the gold answer and printed an all-clear readback:

```
16 checked (rows 4-19) | 16 non-empty | 11 changed
C4 4 int   C5 6 int   C6 12 int   C7 18 int ... C19 34 int
changed: ['C4','C5','C6','C12','C13','C14','C15','C16','C17','C18','C19']
```

C7:C11 are the owner's own hand-filled figures and the rule reproduced **all five exactly**
(18, 26, 32, 26, 14) — the strongest possible corroboration. The agent then spent round 3 on:

```python
# Keep the sheet's established convention for rows without a full 7-day history.
if current - datetime.timedelta(days=7) < first_date:
    ws[f"C{r}"] = wsv[f"C{r}"].value
    continue
```

→ `8 changed`, C4:C6 back to `'n/a'` (str). Grader: *"3 cell(s) hold str where int was expected"* —
exactly those three cells. **The failure is 100% that one line.** The agent's words
("the sheet's established convention") paraphrase the champion's absence-convention clause; and `8`
is exactly the count of cells that were blank on input, which is the number the champion's Round-3
check 3 invites it to drive `len(changed)` towards.

Three distinct defects feed it, and each gets its own edit: (a) the marker-recurrence test is simply
**wrong** — `'n/a'` recurs in C4:C6 so the "keep it" branch fires, and gold overwrites all three
(the owner's own formula is a *shared* formula with `ref="C4:C19"`, uniform over all 16 rows);
(b) the absence convention **contradicts Rule 2**, which already says a marker in a numeric cell is a
wrong answer; (c) nothing makes a post-all-clear write require a reason.

### Cluster 2, root cause (verbatim from the two 50768 traces)

`cand_0004`'s 50768 output is **byte-identical to the passing run's discarded first attempt**. The
difference is that the passing run took a second, label-driven round. Why it could:

- passing Round 1 dumped `A1:H16` (`for c in range(1,9)`, `for r in range(1,17)`) and so printed
  `D12='Impact'` and `F16='Liklihood'` — the two cells that name which axis is which;
- `cand_0004`'s Round 1 printed `A:C` plus `E:H` rows 10–15 only — **column D and row 16 were never
  printed**, so the orientation evidence never entered its context, and it asserted the transpose:
  `# ... columns F:H are Impact 1:3 from F15:H15; rows 12:14 are Likelihood 3:1 from E12:E14.`

One cell decides the task: risk 2 is the *only* entry with Impact ≠ Likelihood, so it lands in `G14`
under the right mapping and `F13` under the transpose. Every other entry is on the (1,1)/(3,3)
diagonal — **including the owner's pre-filled `F14`, which therefore corroborates both orientations
equally and certifies nothing.**

**Attribution verdict.** The scope/pre-filled edits (`cand_0004` A–D) were **never exercised** on
50768: I grepped every assistant message of the failing run for `scope`, `out of scope`,
`already filled`, `worked example`, `re-derive`, `restore`, `original value` — **zero hits**; the
agent overwrote the one pre-filled cell in *both* runs and restored nothing. What `cand_0004`
actually did to 50768 was (i) weaken the Round-3 tripwire that pushed the passing run into a second
round (*"Check this against the printed values, **not against the size of `changed`**"*, plus
*"a later round must not take any cell back off your rule"*), and (ii) spend Round 1's attention on a
four-item scope checklist and a 15-line `<example>` about a dense **column**, in place of the
instruction to print the cells around the box — producing a measurably narrower read.

So: **reship the scope/marker fix; do NOT reship the Round-3 rewrite or the contract's blanket
no-retreat clause; and close the read gap the regression actually came through.**

## Changes kept (7 edits · 2 files · 5 different levers from `guidance/system-prompt/SKILL.md`)

### E1 — `prompt.md` Rule 3: replace the marker-recurrence test with instruction-scope · lever 4 (add a rule with a **stricter** condition) · cluster 1 · BOUNDED

Deletes the bullet *"A pre-filled cell that contradicts your rule is not automatically an example …
If the same marker recurs in the other rows … you keep it"* and the five words *"and leave the
example cells as they are"*; both are replaced by a scope rule with four explicit keep-reasons
(blank/new/remaining scoping · conditional rule false there · column only *read* · value is nothing),
plus **"How often a marker recurs in the column decides nothing"**, plus a new sub-bullet forbidding
an **invented exemption** the instruction never states.

- **VERIFY:** trace 59595 r3 `# Keep the sheet's established convention for rows without a full
  7-day history.` → the recurrence branch the agent took no longer exists, and *"If the instruction
  states no exception, there is none"* names the exact move it made (a self-invented minimum-history
  qualification; the instruction says only "sum from the found date to the date in row 10"). Gold
  confirms the overwrite: the owner's shared formula covers `C4:C19` uniformly.
- **No constraint lost** (SKILL §"Never drop a needed rule"): the dropped *"leave the example cells
  as they are"* reappears as keep-reasons 1–4, with conditions attached.
- **BLAST RADIUS / SAFE:** only **2 of 39** passing tasks genuinely preserve a pre-filled in-range
  cell, and both are protected by a named keep-reason: **80-42** (*"into the first available,
  **blank** rows"* = reason 1 almost verbatim; its trace finds `start_row = 4000` by scanning for
  blankness and never consults the marker heuristic at all) and **142-12** (reasons 2 + 3 — its rule
  is conditional and `G:J` are read-only). **53647** is reason 4 (gold `E15` empty). The other 15
  preserve-*looking* tasks (2768, 37378, 382-10, 38462, 39046, 416-15, 463-17, 47798, 48588, 48921,
  50768, 53383, 54144, 59196, 9569) assign every in-scope cell themselves — the pre-fill only *looks*
  untouched because the recomputed value is identical, so no flip is possible. Positive precedents:
  **39046** recomputes a pre-filled `F4=0` (the textbook "recurring 0 marker"), **59196** overwrites
  a *correct* pre-filled `H3='D'`, **9569** overwrites the owner's rounded `AO9=0.1707` — all pass.
  Independent corroboration: this edit's `cand_0004` ancestor shipped and **38/40 held at 1.0**.

### E2 — `prompt.md` Rule 3: bound the absence convention · lever 3 (consolidate a contradiction) · cluster 1 · BOUNDED

Appends: it settles what you write *into* a row whose value is genuinely absent, and *"is never a
reason to leave a marker standing in a cell your rule prescribes a real number for — as Rule 2 says,
a marker sitting in a cell whose answer is a number is a wrong answer, not an empty one."*

- **VERIFY:** this is the clause the agent's words *"the sheet's established convention"* paraphrase.
  It was in live contradiction with Rule 2's *"a marker left sitting in that cell is a wrong answer,
  not an empty one"* — the two gave opposite verdicts on `C4='n/a'`. Resolved toward the stricter.
- **BLAST RADIUS:** the convention itself is **kept intact** for the case it was written for (80-42,
  which must match the table's `'None'`/`'N/A'` spelling in rows it is *filling*). Narrowing only.

### E3 — `task_template.md` Round 1: same correction in the file the agent reads most · lever 1 (rewrite positively) · cluster 1 · BOUNDED

Replaces *"leave the example cell as it is"* + the odd-one-out/whole-column marker bullet with: check
your rule against it, **then write your rule's value into it like any other cell the rule covers**;
leaving it alone is right only under the four named scope reasons; *"It already had something in it"*
is not one, *"and neither is how many rows share a marker: three `n/a`s in a column of sixteen
otherwise-computed numbers are placeholders, and so are sixteen, if the rule reaches them."*

- **VERIFY:** `task_template` is ~60% of the agent's words and carried the *same* wrong recurrence
  test as `prompt.md`; fixing only one file leaves the agent a sentence to fall back on.
- **Deliberately NOT done:** no restructure of Round 1 into a scope checklist and **no added
  `<example>`.** That is precisely the `cand_0004` change whose observable effect was a narrower
  Round-1 read on 50768. This edit keeps Round 1's shape and its read instructions.

### E4 — `task_template.md` Round-3 check 3: additive clarification, **nothing deleted** · lever 8 (tighten the output contract) · cluster 1 · BOUNDED

Check 3's two-sided test is kept **verbatim** (it is the tripwire 50768 needs). Appended: judge cell
by cell against scope, never by a count; a cell that arrived holding a **marker or stale value inside
a range the rule covers** is one of the cells you were asked to compute and belongs in `changed`;
*"`len(changed)` is not supposed to equal the number of cells that happened to be blank on input"*;
and a covered cell already holding your rule's value is absent from `changed` — that is agreement.

- **VERIFY:** 59595 drove `changed` from 11 to exactly **8 = the number of originally-blank cells**.
  This names that number as the wrong target, without weakening the over-reach half.
- **BLAST RADIUS:** this is where `cand_0004` went wrong and I did the opposite. It replaced check 3
  with *"not against the size of `changed`"*; I **keep** *"If it is larger … if it is smaller …"* and
  only add a condition ("arrived holding a marker or a stale value, inside a range the rule covers").
  142-12's preserved cells are neither markers nor stale, so its verdict is unchanged; 37378 (passes
  with `changed: ['A4']`, 1 of 5 in-scope cells, the rest already equal) gains an explicit all-clear.

### E5 — `task_template.md` interaction contract: a later write needs a printed reason · lever 6 (restructure into an ordered precondition) · cluster 1 · BOUNDED

*"Every round that writes to the file after the first must be justified by something you printed."*
Because replies carry no prose, the justification goes in a first-line comment: which of the four
checks came out wrong, or which cell you printed contradicts your rule. **If you cannot name one,
the task is over — reply with no code block.** Then: recompute the whole range from the pristine
input under the corrected rule — *"that is how you move a value out of the wrong box of a grid into
the right one, and `changed` may legitimately come back with different members than before."* What is
never a correction is **putting a cell's own original content back** — `ws[a1] = wsv[a1].value` —
*"so `changed` may change membership between rounds, but it must not shrink because you restored
originals."*

- **VERIFY (structural):** the skipped step is now a **precondition** of the thing the agent must do
  next (emit a block), not advice placed earlier. The champion already says *"Once the readback
  matches what you intended, stop"* — the agent has that rule and skipped it, so this is STRUCTURE,
  not another sentence of emphasis. It also names the exact failing idiom: 59595's losing line is
  literally `ws[f"C{r}"] = wsv[f"C{r}"].value`.
- **BLAST RADIUS — this is the clause `cand_0004` got wrong and the one I rescoped.** `cand_0004`
  said *"a later round must not take any cell back off your rule"*, full stop; that reads as a ban on
  the corrective second round. Mine **explicitly blesses** it ("move a value out of the wrong box of
  a grid into the right one"; "`changed` may change membership"). Audited mechanically over all 40
  champion traces: 7 passing tasks write twice — **267-18, 2768, 382-10, 43436, 50768, 54144,
  59196** — and in every one `changed` either holds size (2768 9→9, 43436 15→15, **50768 2→2 with
  different members** — the orientation fix, which this text names as legitimate) or grows (59196
  1→2). **No passing task's `changed` ever shrinks. 59595 is the only trace in the run where it
  does** (11→8). The discriminating condition is therefore exactly the one I wrote, and it is
  satisfiable for 50768: its correcting round's own comment is *"Diagnostic: matrix labels show rows
  E12:E14 = Impact 3,2,1 and columns F15:H15 = Liklihood 1,2,3"* — a printed cell contradicting its
  rule, i.e. a valid first-line justification.

### E6 — `prompt.md` Rule 3: read the axis TITLES; corroborate on an asymmetric entry · lever 4 + a worked method · cluster 2 · BOUNDED

New bullet after the existing axis-label bullet: a label strip gives the *levels*, not what they
measure; the naming word sits **one cell further out** — corner column beside the label column, or
the row just under the label row — **outside `answer_position` and outside the preview**; dump every
cell of the block containing the box and its labels before deciding the mapping; and *"it is
invisible in every entry whose two coordinates happen to be equal — so test your mapping on an entry
whose coordinates **differ**. An entry that agrees under both orientations confirms nothing."*
Mirrored as one clause in `task_template` Round 1's read list and in Round-3 check 4.

- **VERIFY:** `cand_0004`'s 50768 Round 1 printed `A:C` + `E10:H15` and so never saw `D12='Impact'`
  / `F16='Liklihood'`; the passing run dumped `A1:H16` and saw both, then corrected the transpose
  citing exactly those labels. The existing bullet already says *"print those row and column labels"*
  — the agent **did** print the label strips and still got it wrong, because the strips are not the
  evidence; the **titles** are, and they sit outside the window the old wording describes. That is a
  genuine METHOD/KNOWLEDGE gap, not a repeated rule. The symmetry clause is verified against check 4
  directly: 50768's pre-filled `F14` sits at (1,1), satisfies check 4 under *both* orientations, and
  so certified the wrong answer — the one documented way check 4 can certify a wrong answer.
- **HONESTY NOTE (the REAL test):** 50768 currently scores 1.0, so this edit does not target a
  task failing *today*. I am shipping it as **regression-hardening for the blast radius I am
  entering**: 50768 is the only task in this run to have been broken **twice** (`cand_0002` and
  `cand_0004`), its passing run needed a second round to get there, and the single cell that decides
  it is invisible to every check the prompt currently describes. The edit can only make the agent
  print *more* in Round 1 and test its mapping *harder*; it removes nothing and gates nothing.

### E7 — both files: bound *"a row of markers … wins where the two disagree"* · lever 3 (resolve a contradiction) · cluster 1 · BOUNDED

Appends to the "where the prose is loose, the sheet is precise" paragraph in each file: what the
header / worked formula / row of markers settles is how to **read** the instruction — which column,
which criterion, which type, how that table writes absence — *not which cells your rule is
responsible for*.

- **VERIFY:** as written, *"a row of markers … wins where the two disagree"* is a third sentence that
  licenses keeping `'n/a'`, now in direct conflict with E1/E2. SKILL §"Resolve conflicts, don't stack
  rules" requires listing every rule governing one action and removing the disagreement. Nothing is
  deleted; the sentence keeps its full force over *reading*.

## What I deliberately did NOT do

- **Did not reship `cand_0004`'s Round-3 check-3 rewrite** (*"not against the size of `changed`"*) or
  its contract clause *"a later round must not take any cell back off your rule"*. Those are the
  edits whose removal of the second-round tripwire I attributed to `broke={50768}`. (E4 and E5 cover
  the same cluster additively, and E5 explicitly permits the corrective round.)
- **Did not reship `cand_0004`'s Round-1 restructure or its `<example>`.** Measured side effect: a
  narrower Round-1 read on the task that regressed.
- **Did not re-test anything in `cand_0002`'s `broke={402-43, 50768, 80-42}`**: no `PLAN`/`LEAVE`
  dicts, no `assert not offplan`, no Round-3 verdict table, no `if cell.value is None` ban (E1's
  keep-reason 1 states the *opposite*, which is what 80-42 needs), no `ws.max_row` clip, no prose
  `ANCHOR:` conclusion requirement.
- **Did not touch the anchor text or the never-round rules** (`cand_0003`'s `fixed={560-12, 9569}`).
  They work; no edit here is adjacent to them.
- **Skipped again, for the third iteration, two statements I believe are FALSE but which no failing
  task implicates:** `prompt.md`'s *"never rename, add, remove or reorder sheets"* (passing tasks
  **395-36** and **402-43** both add a sheet and pass anyway) and the Rule 2 table row implying the
  text `"42"` never works for a number (the grader `float()`-parses it). Both fail the REAL test, and
  on the last iteration of a run a clean single-cluster diff is worth more at the gate than a correct
  edit with no measurable effect beside it. Flagged in INSIGHTS for any future run.
- **No type-homogeneity assert in Round 3** — refuted: it would fire on 80-42, whose graded box
  legitimately mixes `datetime`/`int`/`bool`/`'None'`/`'N/A'`.

## Breadth: why 7 edits and not more

There is exactly **one** failing task on val. Breadth in the sense of "more failing clusters" is not
available — the 7 edits are the three independent defects behind cluster 1 (wrong discriminator ·
contradicted convention · unguarded post-all-clear write), each in both files where it appears, plus
the regression channel. Every additional edit I considered either failed the REAL test (the two
false statements above) or had been refuted by a prior RESULT. On a 0.0072 bar with 39/40 already
passing, a speculative eighth edit has negative expected value.

## Prompt size

`prompt.md` 12051 → 14671 chars; `task_template.md` 10462 → 13457. Growth is entirely the fix set;
two pieces of text were removed (the recurrence bullet, *"leave the example cells as they are"*) with
every constraint they carried relocated into E1's keep-reasons. Per SKILL §"Watch length, but measure
it": if this candidate is accepted and the next run plateaus, prune from the two false statements
above first — they cost words and carry no verified constraint.

## Process / agent features used

Parallel read-only subagents (`guidance/optimizer/claude-code.md`), three at once, each handed one
artifact and told to quote verbatim: (1) 59595's failing champion trace, (2) 50768's passing champion
trace, (3) a side-by-side of 50768 under `cand_0003` vs `cand_0004`. Subagent (3) **overturned my
working hypothesis** — I had pre-registered "the no-retreat clause blocked 50768's orientation fix"
and the trace showed the real mechanism was an unprinted axis title plus a de-fanged check 3. I then
ran one mechanical audit myself (save-count + `changed`-sequence across all 40 traces) to convert
that into the quantitative blast-radius claim in E5. Writing the prose edits was not parallelised:
all seven touch two files and one cluster, and merging concurrent edits to overlapping prose costs
more than it saves.
